transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um... I guess I'm here because... well, I just don't care about anything anymore. Like, nothing at all. It's actually really sad if I think about it too much, but mostly I just feel completely blank. I used to be so involved in things, you know? I was taking these community art classes—watercolor mostly, a little acrylic, every Tuesday night, and I haven't been in months. My brushes are just gathering dust on my desk. And then there were my board-game nights with my friends on Thursdays, we used to play all these long strategy games, and they keep texting me to come over, but I just... I can't bring myself to care. I just leave them on read. 

I used to be so active, too. I loved hiking, going up to the trails on the weekends just to get out of the house, and I was supposed to be getting back to my recreational soccer team this season. I played midfield for a couple of years. But the thought of putting on my cleats or even walking out the front door just feels completely pointless now. I can't even fathom trying to run around a field. Now I just sit in my room. That's literally all I do. I just sit on my bed, sometimes not even looking at my phone or watching TV, just sitting there while my whole life, all the things that used to make me who I am, just completely slip away. And I just sit in my room and let it happen because I don't have it in me to care anymore.
How long has it been since you started feeling this way—when did you first notice you stopped caring about these activities?

Well, it's... it's hard to pin down the exact day, you know? Because it wasn't like I just woke up one morning and decided I didn't care about anything. It kind of crept up on me. But if I really think about it, I guess... well, I remember it was getting really bad around the summer of last year. Yeah, definitely last summer. Because I remember I had bought this new set of hiking boots—these really nice, waterproof ones that I had saved up for—and they arrived in June, I think. And I opened the box, and they smelled like new leather and rubber, and I just looked at them and felt... nothing. Just this heavy, gray nothingness. I didn't even try them on. I just pushed the box into the corner of my closet. 

And from that point on, it just became this constant, everyday thing. It's been like that ever since. So, from last summer until now... that makes it about a year and four months, I think? A year and four months of just... waking up and wishing I hadn't. Wishing I could just stay asleep because being awake means having to face the fact that I don't care about anything. I remember my birthday was in August last year, and my mom tried to take me out to this nice Italian place we used to go to, and I just sat there staring at my pasta, unable to even lift my fork because it just felt so exhausting and pointless. And it hasn't let up since then. Not for a single day in the last sixteen months. It's just this endless, flat line.
Do you have any diagnosed medical conditions, neurological issues, or are you taking any medications or substances that started around the same time your mood changed?

No, no, nothing like that. I've never really had any major health problems, you know? Like, physically, I've always been pretty okay. I mean, I get the occasional cold or sinus infection in the winter, especially when the weather changes, but nothing chronic. No neurological stuff, definitely not. My brain... well, physically, my brain is fine, I guess. I haven't hit my head or been in any accidents or anything like that. And I'm not taking any medications either. My mom actually asked me the same thing a few months ago, she was like, "Are you sure you didn't start taking some new allergy pill or something that's making you feel this way?" But I haven't. I don't even take Tylenol unless I absolutely have to, like if I have a really bad headache that won't go away after drinking water and lying down in a dark room. 

And as for substances... no. I don't do drugs. I used to drink socially, you know, maybe a glass of wine or two when I'd go out with my friends for board-game night, or maybe a beer after a soccer game with the team, just to celebrate or unwind. But I haven't even done that since all this started. I just don't have the desire to drink. It doesn't sound appealing at all. The thought of alcohol just makes my stomach feel heavy. So, yeah, there was no new medication, no new medical diagnosis, no drugs, nothing that changed right before last summer. It was just... just me, living my normal life, and then slowly, everything just drained out of it. There's no physical reason for it that I know of. I wish there was, honestly. Because if it was a pill causing it, I could just stop taking the pill, right? But it's not. It's just... me.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself, or thoughts that you would be better off dead?

Well, yeah... I mean, I kind of mentioned it before, about wishing I hadn't woken up. But it's... it's more than just a passing thought now. It's like this constant, heavy blanket over everything. I just keep having these thoughts that I don't want to wake up anymore. Every night when I go to sleep, there's this little part of me that just hopes I'll slip away quietly and not have to open my eyes to another gray day where nothing matters. It's so exhausting, you know? Just the act of existing. 

And it actually got really bad a few weeks ago. My friend, the one who always tries to get me to come to board-game nights, she got worried because I hadn't answered her texts in like a week. So she actually used her spare key—I gave her one years ago when she watered my plants while I was visiting my aunt in Ohio—and she just let herself in. And... well, she found me sitting on the floor of my bedroom. I hadn't showered in days, the room was a mess, clothes everywhere, and I was just rocking back and forth. And she told me later that when she walked in, I was actually saying it out loud. I didn't even realize I was doing it, but I was just repeating, "I can't keep living like this. I can't keep living like this." Over and over. It terrified her. It terrified me, honestly, when she told me. Because I really meant it. I just... I don't see the point of continuing when every single day is just this unbearable, empty weight. I haven't made a plan or anything, like I haven't bought anything to hurt myself, but the feeling that I'd be better off if everything just stopped... it's there all the time. Just constantly playing in the back of my mind like a radio left on in another room.

Have you experienced anything like hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or having beliefs—like feeling you're being punished, worthless in a way that feels beyond just sad, or that something unusual is happening—that others tell you aren't true?

Well... yeah, actually. I didn't know if I should bring it up, because it sounds so crazy, but... since you're asking. It started a little while ago, and it's... it's really unsettling. It's not just a thought in my head, you know? It's not like my own inner monologue being mean to me. It's an actual voice. A woman's voice. And it always comes from the same place—the corner of my bedroom, right by where I pushed that box of hiking boots I told you about. 

I'll just be lying there in bed, staring at the ceiling, feeling that heavy nothingness, and then... I'll hear her. It's as clear as if you were standing right next to my bed speaking to me. It's not muffled or distant. It's sharp. And she always says the same kinds of things. She tells me that I ruined everything. She says, "You ruined it all, you shouldn't even go outside anymore. Just stay inside." Over and over. And the first time it happened, I actually sat up and turned on the lamp because I thought someone had broken into my apartment. I checked the closet, I checked under the bed, I even went out into the hallway with my umbrella like some kind of idiot, but... there was no one there. The apartment was completely locked from the inside. 

But I still hear her. Especially when it gets quiet at night, or when I'm feeling particularly awful about myself. It's like she knows exactly when I'm at my lowest. And it's so confusing because part of me knows there's no one physically in the room, but my ears are hearing it. It's not a feeling, it's a sound. And it just makes me want to pull the covers over my head and never come out, because what if she's right? What if I did ruin everything? I don't even know what "everything" is, but when she says it, it feels so true and so heavy. My friend, the one who came over, she didn't hear it. I asked her, I said, "Did you hear that lady talking?" and she just looked at me with this really sad, scared expression and said no. But I know what I heard. I hear it almost every day now.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a single, continuous depressive episode lasting approximately 16 months, characterized by pervasive anhedonia, loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities (art, board games, hiking, soccer), profound psychomotor and motivational impairment, persistent hopelessness, and passive/active suicidal ideation without a specific plan. Additionally, she reports mood-congruent auditory hallucinations (a critical, accusatory female voice reinforcing themes of guilt and worthlessness—'you ruined it all') occurring specifically during the depressive episode, with no history of manic/hypomanic episodes, substance use, or medical causes. The hallucinations are thematically consistent with depressive cognitive distortions (guilt, worthlessness) rather than bizarre or mood-incongruent psychotic content, supporting a diagnosis of severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms rather than a primary psychotic or schizoaffective disorder. No prior depressive episodes are reported, making this a single episode presentation (F32.3) rather than recurrent (F33.3).
